name: Jet Pilot
variant: The Luau, c. 1958 (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007), p. 130; same spec in Smuggler's Cove (2016), p. 61
notes: Steve Crane's Luau took Don the Beachcomber's Test Pilot frame (lime, grapefruit, cinnamon, falernum, Pernod, bitters) and loaded it with three rums including Lemon Hart 151. Effectively a compact Zombie; blended only about five seconds.

name: Tiki Bowl
variant: Kon-Tiki, Portland (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007); Smuggler's Cove (2016) p. 68 uses 1 oz honey
notes: A single-serving 'bowl' from Crane's hotel Kon-Tiki chain: orange juice and honey soften a three-rum Beachcomber-style base with a 151 kick. Pernod plus Angostura is the same accent pair the Luau used.

name: Cobra
variant: Kon-Tiki, Chicago (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A small, very strong single-rum drink: one ounce of 151 Demerara over equal parts lime, orange and passion fruit syrup, sharpened with Pernod and bitters, then topped with crushed ice.

name: Kon-Tiki Mai Tai
variant: Kon-Tiki, Cleveland (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: Shows how far 'Mai Tai' drifted outside Trader Vic's bars: no orgeat or curaçao, instead a Beachcomber-style honey, orange, ginger and Pernod build. Useful as a name-versus-structure outlier.

name: Lady of Singapore
variant: Kon-Tiki, Portland (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A creamy blended pineapple-coconut drink with dairy and a touch of grenadine, a Kon-Tiki cousin of the Piña Colada from the same era.

name: Derby Daiquiri
variant: Mai-Kai, Mariano Licudine (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
creator: Mariano Licudine
glass: cocktail glass set with a Spanish-comb ice shell
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A frozen daiquiri where orange juice outweighs the lime, served in a coupe framed by one of the Mai-Kai's molded ice shells. The Mai-Kai (opened 1956) kept many Beachcomber techniques alive under ex-Don bartender Mariano Licudine.

name: Last Rites
variant: Mai-Kai, Mariano Licudine (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
creator: Mariano Licudine
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: Three ounces of aged Martinique rum with only light passion fruit and falernum sweetening: a very spirit-heavy Mai-Kai sour.

name: Jamoca
variant: Mariano Licudine (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
creator: Mariano Licudine
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007), p. 144
notes: Coffee as a tiki modifier, a Mariano Licudine signature later seen in the Mai-Kai's Black Magic. The coffee syrup is mapped to brown-sugar syrup since the drink already carries brewed coffee.

name: White Cloud
variant: Mai-Kai (as presented by Make and Drink)
source: Make and Drink (YouTube), catalogued with Sippin' Safari recipes in SBoudrias/cocktails
notes: A small coconut daiquiri with falernum and orange liqueur. Only a secondary transcription was available, so treat the proportions as provisional.

name: Barrel O' Rum
variant: Mai-Kai signature, Atomic Grog tribute reconstruction
creator: Mariano Licudine
source: The Atomic Grog (Jim 'Hurricane' Hayward) tribute recipe, as made by Make and Drink (YouTube)
notes: The Mai-Kai's house signature, likely a descendant of Don the Beachcomber's Rum Barrel; the real recipe is secret. A second Atomic Grog-derived version (Mixing Up Tiki) uses 2 oz each of lime, orange, grapefruit and passion syrup with only 1 tsp honey, so proportions are uncertain.

name: Black Magic
variant: Mai-Kai, Atomic Grog tribute reconstruction
creator: Mariano Licudine
source: The Atomic Grog (Hurricane Hayward) tribute recipe, as made by Make and Drink (YouTube)
notes: A secret Mai-Kai coffee drink; this tribute layers four rums over coffee, honey, citrus, falernum and allspice. The coffee-plus-spice idea follows Mariano's earlier Jamoca.

name: 151 Swizzle
variant: Mai-Kai version, Atomic Grog tribute reconstruction
source: The Atomic Grog (Hurricane Hayward) tribute recipe, as made by Make and Drink (YouTube)
notes: The Mai-Kai's take on the Beachcomber 151 Swizzle adds falernum, grenadine and a little dark Jamaican to the overproof Demerara base.

name: Moonkist Coconut
variant: Mai-Kai (recipe published in Esquire; adapted by Make and Drink)
source: Mai-Kai recipe printed in Esquire, as adapted by Make and Drink (YouTube)
notes: Unsweetened coconut milk plus honey and falernum over three rums: a lighter, spicier coconut drink than the cream-of-coconut colada style.

name: Shrunken Skull
variant: Popular 1:1:1:1 spec (Anders Erickson / Mixing Up Tiki)

ingredients.orig: gold Puerto Rican rum (Don Q Gold)

source: Anders Erickson (YouTube), as transcribed in SBoudrias/cocktails
notes: A skull-mug staple of mid-century menus including the Mai-Kai. The widely circulated spec is simply equal parts lime, grenadine, Demerara and gold rum; origin and original proportions are not documented here.

name: Blue Hawaii
variant: 1957, Harry Yee (Hawaiian Village)
creator: Harry Yee
venue: Kaiser's Hawaiian Village Hotel (later Hilton Hawaiian Village)
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: Created when a Bols representative asked Yee for a drink to sell blue curaçao. A pineapple-and-sour base split between rum and vodka; not the same drink as the later cream-of-coconut Blue Hawaiian.

name: Tropical Itch
variant: Harry Yee, Hawaiian Village Hotel (late 1950s)
creator: Harry Yee
source: Harry Yee's recipe as reported by PUNCH / Imbibe (per Jeff Berry, Yee used no juice other than passion fruit)
notes: Yee's long passion-fruit highball on a bourbon-plus-rum base, served with a bamboo backscratcher to take home. The spirits are sometimes given as 1.5 oz amber 151, and later versions add pineapple and lemon.

name: Mai Tai
variant: Royal Hawaiian Hotel, 1953 (Trader Vic for Matson); spec from 1956 hotel recipe
creator: Victor Bergeron (Trader Vic)

ingredients.orig: dash of curaçao (dash = 1/4 oz per Vic 1972 guide)

source: 1956 Royal Hawaiian recipe as documented by Kevin Crossman, The Search for the Ultimate Mai Tai (ultimatemaitai.com)
notes: Vic's Hawaiian adaptation replaced the long-aged Jamaican rum with light Puerto Rican plus Myers's and trimmed the sweeteners to equal dashes; it had no pineapple or orange juice. The juice-heavy, dark-rum-float Royal Hawaiian Mai Tai served today is a later evolution.

name: Halekulani Cocktail
variant: House Without a Key, Halekulani Hotel, c. 1930s (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
venue: House Without a Key, Halekulani Hotel

ingredients.orig: sugar syrup (in Smuggler's Cove spec; absent from one Sippin' Safari transcription)

source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007); Smuggler's Cove (2016) p. 61
notes: A pre-war Waikiki hotel sour: bourbon with a three-juice mix (lemon, orange, pineapple), grenadine and bitters, served up. A whiskey drink in tropical dress rather than a rum drink.

name: Kamehameha Rum Punch
variant: Hotel King Kamehameha (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A pineapple-led hotel punch with a dark-rum float and just a teaspoon each of grenadine, syrup and blackberry liqueur, typical of the Hawaii resort style.

name: Lovely Lovely
variant: Papeete Bar, Waikikian Hotel, c. 1964 (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
creator: 'Danny' (Papeete Bar)
venue: Papeete Bar, Tahitian Lanai, Waikikian Hotel

ingredients.orig: 2 tablespoons brown sugar (one transcription reads 2 teaspoons)

source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A frozen daiquiri built on 151-proof Puerto Rican rum, split lime and lemon, and brown sugar. The sugar reads as 2 tbsp in one transcription and 2 tsp in another; tablespoons fits the 2 oz of citrus.

name: Mauna Kea Kiaha
variant: Batik Bar, Mauna Kea Beach Hotel (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
venue: Batik Bar, Mauna Kea Beach Hotel
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: Coconut two ways (sweetened cream and unsweetened milk) with coffee liqueur and no citrus at all, an unusual acid-free resort drink.

name: Pahoehoe
variant: Batik Bar, Mauna Kea Beach Hotel (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
venue: Batik Bar, Mauna Kea Beach Hotel
glass: double old fashioned or small tiki bowl
garnish: flaming lemon shell with sugar cube and 151 rum
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: Rum, passion fruit, lemon and grenadine, the Hurricane's flavor profile in a short glass, finished with a flaming lemon shell. Named for the smooth lava found around the hotel.

name: Sleeping Giant
variant: Lagoon Cocktail Terrace, Coco Palms Resort, c. 1960s (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
venue: Lagoon Cocktail Terrace, Coco Palms Resort
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: An orange-pineapple rum cooler with a little orgeat and sour mix, named for the ridge above the Coco Palms. Very low acid, which is typical of the island resort style.

name: Bali Hai
variant: House of Happy Talk, Hanalei Plantation, early 1960s (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
venue: House of Happy Talk, Hanalei Plantation

ingredients.orig: Hanalei house mix (2 oz total: 3 lemon : 1 each orange, pineapple, guava nectar, orgeat : 1/4 each passion fruit juice, simple)

source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007), from the California Bartenders Guild magazine Good Taste; house-mix proportions per teekee-deebee
notes: A sparkling hotel punch: rum and a lemon-heavy house juice mix topped with Champagne. Another version uses okolehao, lime, lemon and simple syrup, so the spec is uncertain. The mix is expanded into its parts here.

name: Hanalei Rum Punch
variant: House of Happy Talk, Hanalei Plantation, early 1960s (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
venue: House of Happy Talk, Hanalei Plantation
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007); house-mix proportions per teekee-deebee
notes: Fresh pineapple and banana blended with the Hanalei house mix, curaçao and rum, poured over ice and finished with a spoon of dark rum. It shares its uncertain house mix with the hotel's Bali Hai.

name: Mr. Bali Hai
variant: Bali Hai restaurant (Berry, Beachbum Berry Remixed)
location: Shelter Island, San Diego, California, USA
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry Remixed (2010)
notes: The house drink of the Bali Hai on Shelter Island, which is still open: dark and light rum with pineapple and lemon, plus coffee liqueur. Coffee as a tiki modifier shows up again in the Mai-Kai's Jamoca and Black Magic.

name: Tropical Itch
variant: Bali Hai, San Diego (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
location: Shelter Island, San Diego, California, USA
garnish: mango slice speared on a bamboo backscratcher
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A different drink from Harry Yee's Tropical Itch that keeps the backscratcher gimmick: gin and light rum with mango, cinnamon and a hint of almond.

name: Hawaiian Sunset
variant: Aku Aku, Stardust Hotel (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
venue: Aku Aku Polynesian Restaurant, Stardust Hotel
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007); identical in Smuggler's Cove (2016) p. 62
notes: A vodka sour sweetened with orgeat and a little grenadine, served up. It shows vodka showing up on Polynesian menus by 1960.

name: Aku-Aku Gold Cup
variant: Aku Aku, Stardust Hotel (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
venue: Aku Aku Polynesian Restaurant, Stardust Hotel

ingredients.orig: 1 tsp sugar, dissolved in the lemon juice

source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A falernum-sweetened lemon sour on light rum with a Myers's accent, strained over a molded ice shell like the Mai-Kai's.

name: Sidewinder's Fang
variant: The Lanai, c. 1960s (Smuggler's Cove spec)
glass: large snifter lined with a spiral orange peel
source: Martin & Rebecca Cate, Smuggler's Cove (2016), p. 62 (drink documented in Beachbum Berry Remixed)
notes: A long, sour-sweet passion fruit and citrus rum drink stretched with seltzer, presented with an orange peel carved into a snake. Equal parts lime, orange and passion syrup make it a clean 1:1:1 template.

name: Port Light
variant: Kahiki Supper Club version (as presented by Mixing Up Tiki)
source: Mixing Up Tiki (YouTube), Kahiki version, as transcribed in SBoudrias/cocktails
notes: A bourbon, lemon and passion fruit sour, one of the few whiskey drinks on classic tiki menus. Attribution is disputed (one database credits Trader Vic). Smuggler's Cove's modern version uses 2 oz bourbon, 1 oz lemon, 0.75 oz honey, 0.5 oz passion fruit and egg white.

name: Ray's Mistake
variant: Tiki-Ti, 1968: amateur reconstruction (the house recipe is secret)
creator: Ray Buhen
source: Ian Moerson, 'Making Ray's Mistake' (blog, 2016), via teekee-deebee; origin story per Berry, Sippin' Safari
notes: The Tiki-Ti's best-known drink, said to be born when Ray Buhen used the wrong syrups in an Anting Anting. The recipe is still secret, and Jeff Berry reportedly rejects this reconstruction. Only passion fruit and a dark-rum float are widely agreed on.

name: Hula-Hula
variant: Ray Buhen, Beverly Hills Hotel, 1934 (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
creator: Ray Buhen
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: Created by the Filipino bartender who later founded the Tiki-Ti (1961), in his first bar job. An equal-parts gin, curaçao and orange juice cocktail with no added citrus acid, closer to an Orange Blossom than a tiki sour.

name: Scorpion
variant: Kelbo's, Hank Riddle, 1950s (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
creator: Hank Riddle
location: Fairfax Avenue, Los Angeles, California, USA
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A single-serving version of Trader Vic's Scorpion bowl: it keeps the brandy-gin-rum and orgeat core but uses lime and adds passion fruit.

name: Polynesian Guava Daiquiri
variant: Kelbo's, Hank Riddle, 1950s (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
creator: Hank Riddle
location: Fairfax Avenue, Los Angeles, California, USA
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: Despite the name it is a gin drink: guava nectar and lime with a teaspoon of crème de banane, flash-blended.

name: Tiger Shark
variant: The China Trader, 1950s, per Tony Ramos (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
creator: Tony Ramos (recorded)
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A three-rum pineapple daiquiri blended briefly and strained. Recorded by ex-Beachcomber bartender Tony Ramos from the China Trader, where the Hawaiian Eye TV crew drank.

name: Merciless Virgin
variant: Skipper Kent's, 1942–1967 (Smuggler's Cove spec)
creator: Frank 'Skipper' Kent
source: Martin & Rebecca Cate, Smuggler's Cove (2016), p. 67, from the collection of Jacqueline Zumwalt
notes: From Trader Vic's San Francisco rival Skipper Kent: a lemon rum sour sweetened entirely by liqueurs (Cherry Heering, falernum, curaçao). One transcription gives 0.75 oz curaçao instead of 0.25.

name: Captain's Grog
variant: Captain's Inn, c. 1962 (Berry, Remixed; same in Smuggler's Cove)
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry Remixed (2010); Smuggler's Cove (2016), p. 65
notes: A grog sweetened with maple syrup, a rare tiki sweetener, with vanilla and almond extracts, falernum and curaçao over three rums, lengthened with seltzer.

name: Suffering Bastard
variant: 1942, Joe Scialom (from his papers, via Berry, Remixed)
creator: Joe Scialom
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry Remixed (2010), from Scialom papers lent by his daughter Colette
notes: A wartime hangover cure for Allied officers: gin and brandy with lime cordial, bitters and ginger beer. The IBA and Smuggler's Cove use 0.5 oz fresh lime (Smuggler's adds 0.25 oz demerara syrup), and bourbon often replaces the brandy. Unrelated to Trader Vic's later rum drink of the same name.

name: Dead Bastard
variant: Joe Scialom four-spirit escalation (via Berry, Remixed)
creator: Joe Scialom
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry Remixed (2010), as made by Cocktail Virgin Slut (2016)
notes: The joke sequel to the Suffering Bastard: four spirits at half an ounce each, so the total alcohol matches the two-spirit original. The Dying Bastard (three spirits) sits between the two.

name: Cou-Cou-Comber
variant: Joe Scialom, Caribe Hilton (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
creator: Joe Scialom

ingredients.orig: served in (and eaten from) a hollowed-out cucumber

source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: Scialom's post-Cairo gimmick for Hilton in the late 1950s: a dry vodka sour with Pernod, served in a cucumber you eat as you drink.

name: Bali Bali
variant: Bali Ha'i at the Beach, New Orleans (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
venue: Bali Ha'i at the Beach (Pontchartrain Beach)
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A four-spirit tall punch (Jamaican and light rum, gin, Cognac) over a three-juice, passion and falernum base, from the amusement-park Polynesian restaurant at Pontchartrain Beach.

name: Samoan Typhoon
variant: Joe King Sui, Hawaiian Village, Tampa (Berry, Sippin' Safari)
creator: Joe King Sui

ingredients.orig: 1 oz honey (straight), expressed as 1:1 honey mix

source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry's Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A two-serving blended punch from a Florida Polynesian motel restaurant, heavy on lime with honey and passion fruit. The straight honey is doubled here to express it as 1:1 honey mix.

name: Saturn
variant: 1967, J. 'Popo' Galsini (Berry, Beachbum Berry Remixed)
creator: J. 'Popo' Galsini
venue: California Bartenders' Guild entry, IBA world championship (winner)
glass: pilsner (often served in a coupe today)
garnish: lemon peel ring around a cherry
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry Remixed (2010)
notes: A rare gin-based tiki classic that won the 1967 world bartending championship: passion fruit, falernum and orgeat over London dry gin. It was originally blended; Smuggler's Cove shakes it with 0.75 oz lemon. The garnish rings a cherry with lemon peel to suggest the planet.

name: Jungle Bird
variant: Kuala Lumpur Hilton original (Poister 1989; Berry, Intoxica 2002)
creator: Jeffrey Ong
source: Kuala Lumpur Hilton recipe via John J. Poister, The New American Bartender's Guide (1989); reprinted by Jeff Berry, Intoxica! (2002)
notes: Beverage manager Jeffrey Ong created it as the welcome drink for the KL Hilton's July 1973 opening; it is often misdated to 1978. The original is a long, pineapple-dominant drink with Campari as the bitter accent. The 2000s craft version (Giuseppe González) cut the pineapple to 1.5 oz and used blackstrap rum.
